Kernel Note By definition, ω is not only the smallest successor-inductive ordinal, but also the ⊆-minimal (least) element among all successor-inductive (Peano-inductive) classes in the subclass (⊆) order (Ind(ω) ∧ ∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (ω ⊆ Q)), directly expressing simple countable mathematical (Peano) induction up to ω. | Special Def.: ω = ⋂{q | Ind(q)}; General Def.: ∀(x:Class), (x ∈ ω) ⟷ (∀(Q:Class), Ind(Q) —→ (x ∈ Q)).

0(forall([phi@Variable]:[Fm@Type])((Fau,[]|-[phi@Fm.Expression])-->eval([phi@Fm.Expression])))
Kernel Note Soundness of the non-recursively-enumerable (non-r.e.) Henkin completion 𝘍: if (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ), then ⟦φ⟧ holds in the fixed background model M. Why this avoids Tarski and Löb inconsistency: While the r.e. base theory 𝘛 cannot assert its own soundness without violating Gödel's second incompleteness theorem and Löb's theorem (hence soundness of 𝘛 is not postulated in 𝘛), the full theory 𝘍 is non-r.e. and Henkin-complete (Th(M)). The evaluation operator ⟦φ⟧ lives in the +1 metalogic on the base formula sublanguage Fm₀ without self-referential truth predicate internalisation, avoiding Tarski undefinability.

Kernel Note Semantic completeness of the non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍: for every sentence φ, if φ evaluates to true in the background model M (⟦φ⟧), then φ is formally derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). Together with Soundness of 𝘍 (3.72), this establishes (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ⇔ ⟦φ⟧, identifying 𝘍 as the complete true theory Th(M).

Kernel Note Syntactic negation-completeness of the non-r.e. Henkin completion 𝘍: for every sentence φ, if ¬φ is not derivable in 𝘍 (¬(𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ)), then φ is derivable in 𝘍 (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ). In classical logic, this is equivalent to (𝘍, [] ⊢ φ) ∨ (𝘍, [] ⊢ ¬φ). In the bivalent semantics of the background model M (⟦φ⟧ ∨ ⟦¬φ⟧), negation-completeness follows directly from semantic completeness and soundness.

Kernel Note If a formula < 𝘍,Γ⊢𝛗> is derived in 𝘍 from the empty context, then the formula 𝛗 is derived in 𝘍 from the context Γ. Why this holds for 𝘍: for an arbitrary theory 𝘞, concluding (𝘞, Γ⊢𝛗) from (𝘞, [] ⊢ <𝘞, Γ⊢𝛗>) requires 1-consistency / Σ₁-soundness of 𝘞 (and for the r.e. base theory 𝘛, asserting internal co-necessitation would by Löb's theorem 5.01 trivialize 𝘛). Because 𝘍 is a non-r.e. sound Henkin extension equipped with Soundness 3.73 ((𝘍, [] ⊢ ψ) → ⟦ψ⟧), instantiating 3.73 at ψ := <𝘍, Γ⊢𝛗> directly yields (𝘍, Γ⊢𝛗).
